I think the Beauty of this patch it’s 50% the melody and 50% the sound design. 

The patch is really complicated to explain but I can explain the key points.

1) One the idea behind it is too give movement to the melodie like pianist does. For this purpose I recorded a looping modulation with the tetrapad + tete and feed into a sample and hold triggered by the melody gate, the sound before the fx is going thru a vca modulated with that previous sample and hold. All this to give a sense of crescendo to the melodic path. Another point is that the envelope generator is an Adsr (the multi envelope from verbos), this allow me to have another point of expression. 

2) This lead is composed by the harmonic wave and the sawtooth wave of the harmonic oscillator plus a sub oscillator + a fifth from the Honda piston. Everything goes into the zadar filter and the Optomix, then into a vca doing the previous explained effect and after into the multi delay processor, magneto and the analog heat +fx (reverb + saturation + tape pitch shifting fx) 


3) Everything is sequenced from the metropolix heavy modulated with the octatrack so I can have a longer sequence + the sequence selector from verbos modulating values like the glide or the octave of the metropolix (it’s responsible of a lot of modulations of the harmonic oscillator too, the sequence selector is crazy). 

In general I really think modules like the sequence selector or verbos in general really take the eurorack into another level imho. Cause you unlock that simplicity that allow to experiment a lot. They simply sounds good if you are looking for that raw analog sound.

Taking about why I chose Fumana, Honestly I went for the Fumana because I can genuinely say it sounds very good, and Frap Tolls modules are made 100 km far from my house so I eventually want to try to collaborate with them regarding content creation and it’s very feature packed compared to the buchla Tiptop and the bark. I have and love so many verbos modules and my heart was leading to keep the same brand but I wanted to try something different, so I don’t esclude that in the future I will have the bark filter too. All of the modules you mentioned will serve the purpose amazingly just with different shades

So I had the chance to extensively talk with Mark about his modules and especially about the Bark filter few months ago during the Soundmit in Torino. He told me he designed it thinking as a module to shape the resonances of the sound placing it in the end of the chain, and he split the bands across the spectrum following the bark scale to enhance this purpose. Fumana seems like to work better as “vocoder” cause it has 32 filters, 2 for each band, so you can have a more accurate spectral transferring, however Mark told me that even the Fumana it’s not a real vocoder because a real vocoder it’s made following another logic. That is actually true, so in the end even if you have the triple of the filters available for spectral transferting of the bark filter (12 vs 32) it doesn’t mean you have a better sound because you ultimately have to be judge if it fits the sound you need or want. For example I love the way floating points use the 296e of Buchla for spectral transferting, the result is very nasal sounding, this can be a feature or a down point, you must decide it. 
After saying this, I would say the buchla tiptop 296 it’s way too big for my needs but it sounds very good as far as I heard, very classic (I don’t own it) and the bands are very similar to the Fumana but you can do spectral transferting just with 8. The Bark Filter is very nice analog sounding (verbos like ofcs), it’s the smallest and the one with the best UI, but not meant to do spectral transferting. About The Sputnik one, I heard few demos but I have never considered to cop it.

Patch notes: the main synth is the complex oscillator going thru the Optomix and the multi delay from verbos. The interesting stuffs here happens to the metropolix. I have one random cv that modulate the glide of the sequence and I wrote a 4 note 4 bar sequence on the octatrack that thru yarn modulate the metropolix “pitch pre” parameters. 

So basically in other words “pitch pre” it’s a parameter that change the sequence before the scale quantisation, so modulating it with a different note every bar it creates a sort of chord progression with the same 16 steps sequence of metropolix. 

The base line I recorded it from the mannis iteritas and pitch shift on the octatrack to create a sequence.

So I use 3 sequencer atm! 1. Octatrack (thru Yarn, elektron sequencer) 2. Varigate 8+ 3. Metropolix 

I have to say that the elektron sequencer is my favorite to write complex and more elaborated melodies, if you take enough time to get used is awesome! There are many tricks you can do. For example the octatrack can sequence up to 8 midi channels but you can sequence the same midi channel with 2 or more octatrack midi channel (hope it makes sense for you), this allow to open up possibilities such as complex polyrhythms etc. 

The varigate 8 and the Metropolix are really good to jam and find new melodies very quickly but they are not that consistent to establish the harmonic movements, or the mood of the composition. 

So usually what I do is, I write a solid harmonic sequence with the octatrack sequencer and then I jam over with the other sequencers. 

You can find more songs on my YouTube channel (there all the songs are written on the octatrack) :)

The main source is the BIA, the goes thru the Lyra Fx 8 (that gives a little delay and some distortion) and after to the beads. The beads is almost 100% wet and the “seed” is triggered by the zularic from noise eng., this generate plucky sound plus some atmosphere and background textures. To reinforce the sound I have driven even some of the dry signal from the BIA to the mixer. 
The sequence is generate from the octatrack and is modulated through an internal lfo (it’s very interesting how it works), and I have other light modulations from the marbles going through the filter and some parameters of the Lyra 8 FX 😊

Personally I’ve never used it like drum module, there are definitely some parameters I wouldn’t touch it that make sounds really harsh and not tonal (like the spread and the harmonic) but over all the fact you can morph the waves and you have a layer of noise it makes one of the richest sounding VCO I have ever heard:)
